policy.underwriting: Unchanged V1.9-style direct exposure, event-incremental earnings/cash conversion, expectation, valuation and absorption gates.

reasoning: Easing intensified but the cluster remained too broad; no incremental company order/funding-cost bridge survived without relying on general beta.
Record retail accounts, extreme tech valuations and margin financing made this a crowding/timing risk regime, not a clean fundamental long.
Developer distress plus equity refinancing was real, but no clean A-share absolute earnings catalyst was verified; relative safety is insufficient.
Bull-market equity issuance could repair balance sheets, but no company was frozen where dilution/refinancing created a clearly positive incremental per-share earnings/FCF bridge.

decisions.name: 宝钢股份
reasoning: Bloomberg exposed the extreme iron-ore price decline and domestic high-cost mine pressure; the initial event was not a Baosteel story.
The sector-level implication was ambiguous because steel demand and steel prices were also weak, so v3.3 searched for a company exception rather than promoting the industry.

Baosteel Q1 net profit rose 2.46% while the company itself described the steel sector as returning to losses. Management/analysts attributed resilience to cost reduction and product-mix optimization; high-end automotive/electrical steel supported differentiation.
CICC judged Q1 above its expectation of a YoY decline. At the cutoff the stock still lagged CSI300 by roughly -6.4pp/-7.7pp/-35.8pp over 20/60/120d.
Expectation burden was not empty: CICC forecast 2015 profit +24.5% and about 20x 2015E PE, so this is Research rather than High-priority.
falsifiers: Steel selling prices fall materially faster than ore/other input costs.
Automotive/electrical-steel product mix fails to preserve spreads.
Industry demand deterioration overwhelms company-specific cost/mix advantages.

reasoning: Debt swaps and falling money-market rates were significant, but no company-level new project/credit-loss/earnings bridge was verified without broad infrastructure or bank beta.

Alibaba's mobile traffic/monetization shift was economically important, but no A-share logistics/payment/merchant-service expression had a sufficiently dated and material incremental company bridge in this staging pack.

Industrial policy was large but extremely broad; by mid-June Yicai reported the Industrial 4.0 index had risen about 81% since Mar-10, materially ahead of the market. No fresh company order reset justified paying through the theme crowding.
IPO funding freezes were a market-liquidity event. Brokerage/financial expressions were inseparable from extreme bull-market crowding.

CIPS was a real national financial-infrastructure build, but pre-Q2-cutoff public evidence did not reliably identify an A-share IT vendor with a material CIPS construction contract. Association without supplier proof is rejected.

The industrial-policy opportunity was large, but the direct A-share equipment expression 七星电子 had Q1 revenue -28.3% and negative ex-item earnings. Policy scale had not yet converted into company economics at the cutoff.
Outbound acquisition and European-asset demand were visible, but no company transaction was frozen with a clear technology/channel/cash-flow bridge and acceptable price absorption before quarter-end.
